written_by: Mark · big-move alert (risk gauge back to Risk off)
headline: Stocks keep the Huang bounce, but the risk gauge slips back to Risk off

findings.headline: The rally holds, the defensive side does not let go
findings.body: The S&P 500 is still up about 4.5% at 7,224 and the Euro Stoxx 50 closed up 2.3%, yet the risk gauge has fallen back to -27 (Risk off) from -11 at 15:50. The dollar index is up 0.6% (EUR/USD down 0.8% at 1.089), the US 10-year is higher at 4.94%, VIX is still near 28 and gold is up 4.4% at $3,669, while copper has given back some of its gain against gold in the last hour. Equities are buying the Nvidia news but rates, the dollar and volatility are not yet signing off on it.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

findings.headline: Nvidia brings Huang back and the AI trade gets its anchor back
findings.body: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director with immediate effect, after President Trump publicly called for his return, and the stock jumped about 30% at the open. Last week's rout was as much about who runs the AI bellwether as about AI spending, so this removes the biggest single overhang without settling the capex debate. Tech is leading and defensives such as staples are lagging, which is what a short-covering reset looks like.

findings.headline: Washington leans on the Fed before its December decision
findings.body: On Face the Nation, Treasury Secretary Bessent warned the Fed risks overtightening, pointing to hawkish comments from Fed officials and a sharp tightening in financial conditions, and Bill Ackman made the same case. The first tests come today: the 2-year note auction at 19:00 Zurich and a speech by New York Fed President Williams at 22:00 Zurich, then the US inflation data due before Thanksgiving. A softer Williams would do more for this rally than the Nvidia news.

findings.headline: The 14:30 data gave the rally no help
findings.body: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index slipped to -0.06 in October from +0.05 in September, with production indicators turning negative and consumption and housing still a drag. It is a small miss, but it backs the argument that the economy is already cooling, which supports the case for the Fed to hold off.

sources.label: Trading Economics: Chicago Fed activity index falls in October

view: Our view: this is a relief rally on a fixed governance problem, not a new AI cycle, so it holds only if the Fed stops leaning hawkish; Williams tonight and the pre-Thanksgiving inflation data will decide whether last week's lows were the bottom.
